LESSON: WATER HARVESTING AND STORAGE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.2: Water Harvesting and Storage

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Water Harvesting and Storage. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we harvest and store water for domestic purposes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WATER HARVESTING AND STORAGE
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Water Harvesting and Storage helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT WATER
We use water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and farming.
Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.
Unsafe water can cause disease — store drinking water in clean covered containers.

PART 1: Discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Water Harvesting and Storage” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Water Harvesting and Storage is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Water Harvesting and Storage” around your school. (skill: discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Water Harvesting and Storage to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Water Harvesting and Storage from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Water Harvesting and Storage: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Water Harvesting and Storage?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we harvest and store water for domestic purposes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Water Harvesting and Storage means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss ways of storing harvested water for domestic use.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
